question: Does the frozen 4:1 five-measurement schedule identify the planted pair more often than evenly spaced sampling under temporally correlated observation noise at 4× marginal noise?
noise: Stationary Gaussian AR(1) on the original grid with 30 time points: correlation rho at lag 0.2 and rho^|i-j| at other grid lags. Generate two independent contrast errors per draw, each SD sqrt(2) × 0.06 as from independent treated and control arms. The same full-grid contrast is sampled by both schedules, and error innovations are paired across rho. Only post-shutoff observation noise changes. Marginal noise variance stays fixed. No nugget or cross-record dependence.
scoring: Use closest concatenated two-record trace among ten unordered source pairs; try both globally consistent orientations with reversed pulse amplitudes in record 2, fractional ties within 1e-10 in standardized squared distance. Run the unchanged Euclidean scorer and a covariance-aware scorer using the true marginal covariance submatrix at the five actual times. The latter whitens the observations and frozen templates, with the two records independent. No model fitting, correlation estimation, time reselection or recalibration.
design: Use all 16 previously held-out networks (68101–68116), six targets each, four histories and both stronger-source assignments. Reference comparison uses 4096 paired draws and identical random seeds as the previous study for exact reproduction at rho=0. Three frozen architectures; no target or network exclusions.
inference: The unit is network. At each registered rho and scoring rule compare selected minus even exact-pair accuracy for each of the three models. Simultaneous two-sided 95% paired Student t intervals with Bonferroni adjustment across 51 distinct contrasts (three at rho=0, 48 at eight nonzero rhos across both rules), df=15. Call a schedule advantage or reversal only when the corresponding interval excludes zero; report network wins and conditional Monte Carlo SE separately. Use the grid as tested, without fitting a continuous crossover. Absolute accuracies and covariance-weighted signal energy are descriptive.
checks: Verify original freeze manifests and reproduced target scores at rho=0. Verify unit marginal variance and expected covariance under each sampling policy and independent records. Compare optimized classification to direct 10-dimensional distances using block-diagonal covariance on sampled draws. Independently reconstruct paired intervals from saved target scores.
